name: Move RocksDB write batches to blocking workers

asi.bounded_resources: The same batch, database, write options, admission controls, and durability barriers remain in use. No queue, memory, or concurrency bound changed.
asi.safety: The resolved rocksdb 0.24 binding explicitly marks WriteBatch as Send. Ownership moves into the blocking closure, eliminating an allocation and copy without introducing shared mutation.
asi.summary: Moved RocksDB WriteBatch values directly into blocking workers instead of serializing them into a temporary byte vector and reconstructing them.
asi.validation: Two isolated paired runs were 1.427748x and 1.330330x faster. A fresh 5000-request, concurrency-64 service pair improved from 162.84 to 176.15 writes per second with lower median, 95th-percentile, and 99th-percentile latency.

description: perf(kura): move write batches to blocking workers

name: Remove streaming write buffer zero fill

asi.bounded_resources: The buffer remains capped at 262144 bytes, is reused for all chunks, and remains inside the existing serialized segment append. No queue, concurrency, file-cache, or durability bound changed.
asi.safety: Tokio read_buf initializes only the bytes it reports and safely advances the vector length. The exact-capacity allocation is now fallible and returns an error instead of using an infallible zero-filled allocation.
asi.summary: Large staged writes now read into the reusable vector spare capacity instead of zero-filling the 256-kibibyte segment copy buffer before the source overwrites it.
asi.validation: Paired one-mebibyte streaming-copy benchmarks were 1.206748x and 1.183087x faster. The bounded replicated path integration test passed, including final file-cache release behavior.

description: perf(kura): avoid zeroing streaming write buffers

asi.bounded_resources: Both variants retained the same response-memory semaphore, per-stream send-buffer cap, and 512-stream ceiling. The smaller retained credit is also the tighter transport bound.
asi.decision: Retain the 16-mebibyte fixed connection window. It schedules admitted work more smoothly and remains comfortably above the per-stream window.
asi.finding: A 64-mebibyte connection window released larger response bursts into one HTTP2 connection and reduced throughput while worsening latency.

description: Raise HTTP2 connection window from 16 to 64 MiB

name: Tune bounded segment durability cohort window

asi.decision: Retain the adaptive one-millisecond-per-writer delay capped at 40 milliseconds.
asi.finding: An 8-millisecond cap briefly reduced the first burst latency but formed smaller durability cohorts, causing more filesystem synchronizations and lower sustained throughput.
asi.safety: Both variants kept the same sequence-based durability protocol. The retained setting has the stronger measured batching efficiency without weakening crash ordering or memory bounds.

description: Lower segment durability cohort cap from 40 to 8 ms

name: Reduce bounded HTTP2 per-stream send buffering

asi.bounded_resources: For a 256-kibibyte read, the charged reservation falls from 811008 to 606208 bytes because the transport owner is now physically capped at 65536 bytes. The global response semaphore, transient-memory semaphore, stream ceiling, and bounded waiter queue remain unchanged. Degraded HTTP reads now add the transport cap to their remaining live chunks so the smaller cap cannot under-account them.
asi.safety: Upstream h2 documentation states the limit is per stream and stops polling more capacity once the stream reaches it. The focused transport-lifetime test, degraded-memory tests, production build, and formatting check passed.
asi.summary: Capped each Hyper HTTP2 stream send buffer at 64 kibibytes and changed ByteStream admission from three full chunks to two full chunks plus that explicit send-buffer cap.
asi.validation: Two constrained-memory reversals improved median throughput by about 33.3 and 19.7 percent at concurrency 256. At unconstrained memory the 512-way result was within host variation, about 1.9 percent lower in the immediate median comparison.

description: perf(kura): tighten response send buffering

name: Compare write digests without hex allocation

asi.bounded_resources: The candidate removes one heap allocation per completed write and adds only a fixed 32-byte stack array. No admission, disk, concurrency, or durability behavior changes.
asi.safety: The same computed SHA-256 digest is compared exactly. Focused tests cover equality, mismatch, malformed hexadecimal input, and the wrong encoded length.
asi.summary: Successful ByteStream writes now decode the expected hexadecimal SHA-256 digest into a fixed 32-byte stack array and compare digest bytes directly, instead of allocating and formatting an encoded string from the computed digest.
asi.validation: Two paired runs improved the comparison from roughly 6.63 million per second to 25.93 million or more per second, a minimum 3.845204x speedup.

description: perf(kura): compare write digests without allocation

name: Store one digest copy in parsed blob resources

asi.bounded_resources: Each normal SHA-256 request removes one heap allocation and 64 copied digest bytes. The result remains fully owned and does not borrow request memory.
asi.safety: The range is constructed from the exact blob/ prefix and digest length used to build the key, so both endpoints are valid UTF-8 boundaries. Read and write parser tests passed.
asi.summary: Parsed ByteStream resources now retain the digest as a byte range into their already-owned storage key instead of allocating a second String.
asi.validation: Two paired runs improved isolated resource construction by 1.946463x and 1.996780x.

description: perf(kura): retain one parsed digest copy

name: Resolve successful REAPI write metrics once

asi.bounded_resources: The change adds exactly three fixed metric handles per Metrics registry and removes per-write label allocation. All existing admission, memory, disk, and durability limits are unchanged.
asi.safety: The handles come from the same registered counter and histogram families, so rendered series names and labels are unchanged. The focused rendering test and 5000-write end-to-end run passed.
asi.summary: Successful REAPI writes now update three metric handles resolved once at startup instead of allocating labels and looking up three metric families for every completed write.
asi.validation: Two paired microbenchmarks improved metric recording by 11.720373x and 12.117167x. A fresh-store durable write comparison was within noise at 222.4 versus 223.99 writes per second, with every write successful.

description: perf(kura): pre-resolve successful write metrics

asi.bounded_resources: The change adds one fixed histogram handle and removes per-request heap work. Request admission, inflight tracking, latency sampling, response lifetime, and all resource caps are unchanged.
asi.safety: The handle belongs to the same registered metric family and label set. Focused metric rendering and route ownership tests passed, as did 5000 durable writes per variant.
asi.summary: ByteStream write request accounting now borrows its static route and observes a latency histogram resolved once at startup, eliminating route and label allocations plus a metric-family lookup.
asi.validation: Two paired microbenchmarks improved latency observation by 7.745643x and 8.052481x. End-to-end durable writes remained host-noise-bound; the reverse-order fresh-store pair was 194.24 versus 190.84 writes per second, a 1.75 percent difference.

description: perf(kura): pre-resolve write latency metrics

asi.bounded_resources: The fixed group contains three already-registered metric handles. Per-request state is smaller, while memory reservations, stream staging, decode accounting, concurrency limits, and disk durability are unchanged.
asi.safety: Both rejection paths update the same metric families and labels through pre-resolved handles. The resource-exhaustion metric test passed, as did 10000 durable writes per binary at concurrency 256.
asi.summary: Incoming remote-execution writes now clone one small shared rejection-metrics group instead of the full Metrics aggregate twice while admission ownership is split between request extensions and the body wrapper.
asi.validation: Two paired clone benchmarks improved by 80.187870x and 96.422518x. The exact production binary comparison on 4-kibibyte writes improved from 224.07 to 231.82 writes per second, 3.46 percent, with median latency falling from 705 to 654 milliseconds.

description: perf(kura): narrow write admission metrics

name: Share the metrics aggregate behind one reference

asi.bounded_resources: The wrapper replaces the existing aggregate value with one fixed allocation at startup. It does not add per-request state, change metric cardinality, or alter any memory, stream, disk, or concurrency cap.
asi.safety: All metric objects remain the same thread-safe counters, gauges, histograms, and families. The wrapper is immutable after construction; the size test proves Metrics is one shared reference, and the full metric rendering test passed.
asi.summary: Metrics is now one cloneable shared reference around its immutable aggregate, so stream trackers and background handoffs no longer clone every metric-family handle.
asi.validation: Clone throughput rose from at most 2.531 million to at least 182.115 million per second, a conservative 71.95x speedup. Repeated 500000-request HTTP read samples were within noise at 77775.51 versus 77279.19 reads per second with zero failures and matching median and tail latency.

description: perf(kura): share metrics behind one handle

name: Cache fixed REAPI latency metric handles

asi.bounded_resources: Each metadata method adds one empty OnceLock and creates its existing histogram series only if used. No unused series are allocated, route cardinality remains fixed, and request, memory, disk, and concurrency bounds are unchanged.
asi.safety: Unknown routes retain the owned-label fallback. A focused test verifies the original rendered series and the accounting test verifies every known route is borrowed.
asi.summary: All ten fixed remote-execution protocol routes now borrow static route names. The eight metadata methods resolve their latency histogram lazily once and then update it directly, matching the existing ByteStream fast paths.
asi.validation: Two paired runs improved warm metadata latency observation by 7.924174x and 8.259050x.

description: perf(kura): cache fixed protocol latency metrics

description: test(kura): benchmark bounded connection sharding

asi.bounded_resources: The existing foreground preload reservation still charges every byte. A fixed 32-permit semaphore bounds simultaneous blocking file writes. Memory-pressure and file-cache-dropping paths retain the serial streaming writer and its periodic cache reclamation.
asi.safety: An exclusive segment barrier prevents rotation or synchronization while a positioned range is in progress. A writer publishes its durability sequence only after its complete range is written, and metadata is still committed only after segment synchronization. Concurrent exact-byte reads and non-overlapping ranges are covered by tests.
asi.summary: Small preloaded writes now reserve non-overlapping offsets while briefly holding the segment mutex, then issue bounded positioned writes concurrently.
asi.validation: Three strengthened paired append runs improved by 1.17 to 1.79 times with equivalent physical synchronization counts. Two paired complete artifact-store runs improved throughput by 5.4 and 7.8 percent while reducing median, 95th-percentile, and 99th-percentile latency. Compilation, formatting, positioned-write checks, and concurrent durability checks passed.

description: perf(kura): parallelize bounded segment writes

asi.finding: RocksDB already groups concurrent write batches. Splitting its log and memory-table queues did not produce a repeatable complete-store throughput gain on this workload and made positioned writes slower than the serialized control within both candidate runs.
asi.next: Retain the default ordered write queue and avoid adding a redundant Kura metadata coordinator.
asi.safety: The experiment changed only an established RocksDB ordering-preserving option, but an unproven operational mode is not justified without a clear measured benefit.

description: RocksDB pipelined writes stayed within host noise and worsened paired positioned-write results

asi.bounded_resources: Retain the existing fixed ceiling of 32 positioned writes because it is the smallest measured limit that produced repeatable complete-store gains while keeping concurrent blocking work tightly capped.
asi.finding: Eight and sixteen permits consistently underfilled the storage path. Sixty-four permits improved one heavily contended run but did not repeat the gain and doubles the maximum blocking scheduler and disk pressure.
asi.next: Stop tuning this cap on a shared development host; validate the retained limit on production-shaped Linux hardware before making it configurable.

description: Smaller write caps regressed and sixty-four permits did not repeat its first gain

asi.bounded_resources: The payload was already fully admitted and allocated before this store call. Direct persistence removes temporary-disk reservation and source page-cache occupancy, adds no queue or buffer, and retains the fixed 32-write ceiling plus the cache-reclaiming serial fallback.
asi.safety: File-backed and memory-backed sources share the same namespace and per-artifact locks, precheck, segment durability barrier, metadata commit, outbox reservation, and eviction path. The concurrent restart test exercises the direct path and passed.
asi.summary: Payloads already materialized by bounded Remote Execution batch decoding now enter the existing segment writer directly instead of being written to and reread from a temporary file.
asi.validation: Two paired complete-store runs improved throughput by 31.2 and 32.6 percent. Median latency fell from 32.0 to 18.2 milliseconds and from 36.4 to 22.5 milliseconds; 99th-percentile latency fell from 104.7 to 81.8 milliseconds and from 106.9 to 72.2 milliseconds.

description: perf(kura): persist admitted artifact bytes directly

name: Keep small ByteStream uploads in admitted memory

asi.bounded_resources: The direct buffer replaces temporary-file source pages and is covered by the existing source-plus-destination permit. Allocation failure, oversized uploads, deferred durability, and non-memory sources keep the serial bounded fallback. Positioned writes remain capped at 32 and are limited to 256 kibibytes.
asi.safety: The segment durability barrier completes before page-cache advice, metadata still follows durable bytes, and advice covers only page-aligned full pages inside the writer range. Mixed concurrent file and bounded-memory writes were verified byte-for-byte before and after reopening the store; large fallback, pressure rejection, usage, formatting, compilation, and Clippy checks passed.
asi.summary: Small ByteStream uploads accumulate in one fallibly allocated buffer inside their existing admission reservation and enter the direct segment path. Positioned writers under overlapping cache-reclaiming policy release only their own synchronized range before metadata publication.
asi.validation: Two confirmed end-to-end ByteStream comparisons improved durable throughput by 2.117966 and 1.589157 times. Median latency fell from 95.0 to 42.1 milliseconds and from 71.4 to 39.0 milliseconds; 99th-percentile latency fell from 201.1 to 136.6 milliseconds and from 185.6 to 116.9 milliseconds.

description: perf(kura): bypass staging for small admitted uploads

name: Remove authorization cache-hit allocation and lock overhead

asi.bounded_resources: The change adds a constant fifteen shared metric handles per registry and removes transient allocation from every hit. Cache capacities and all request, memory, and disk admission limits remain unchanged.
asi.safety: The handles belong to the same registered families and exact label sets. Unknown labels retain the previous family lookup path, and focused rendering verifies identical series and counts.
asi.summary: Authorization cache hits update fixed metric handles resolved at startup instead of allocating labels and acquiring three metric-family read locks per request.
asi.validation: Two eight-worker paired runs improved complete cache-hit accounting by 17.973092 and 20.948665 times. Formatting and focused metric tests passed.

description: perf(kura): pre-resolve authorization metrics

name: Minimize authorization key and cache-hit work

asi.bounded_resources: Every cache retains its configured maximum entry count and expiration policy. Fixed 32-byte credential keys replace 64-byte hexadecimal strings, and request contexts retain only one authorization value rather than all headers.
asi.safety: Revocation lookup still runs after every entry lookup with the same ordering. The cache variants share Moka locking, expiration, immediate visibility, and bounded eviction semantics. Focused policy and transport authorization tests passed.
asi.summary: Authorization hits borrow the credential, hash its raw bytes into a fixed binary key, and use synchronous concurrent caches for entries and revocations. Backend consultations retain asynchronous per-key coalescing.
asi.validation: Three eight-worker paired runs improved the complete former key-and-two-cache hit path by 1.238488, 1.275074, and 1.277841 times before the borrowed-key follow-up.

description: Use typed synchronous authorization hit caches

name: Avoid owned authorization entry keys on hits

asi.finding: Avoiding the owned target-key allocation did not improve the concurrent lookup rate. Two paired runs were effectively equal, with one slightly slower.
asi.next: Keep the simpler typed owned key and synchronous bounded caches.
asi.safety: Do not retain the extra Equivalent implementation or direct dependency when they provide no measured benefit.

description: Borrowed entry keys stayed within noise

asi.bounded_resources: All four authorization caches retain the same configured entry ceilings and expiration rules. Production request contexts hold one credential and no unrelated header or query collections.
asi.safety: Every reused decision still performs the revocation lookup in the same order. Borrowed entry keys were measured separately and removed after no gain. Authorization policy, HTTP context, and Remote Execution transport tests passed.
asi.summary: The retained authorization path uses fixed binary credential keys and synchronous bounded caches for hit-only entry and revocation state, while asynchronous per-key consultation coalescing remains on misses.
asi.validation: Final paired confirmations improved the former key construction plus entry and revocation lookup path by 1.172642 and 1.213501 times. Earlier retained-shape runs improved it by 1.238488 to 1.277841 times.

description: perf(kura): confirm streamlined authorization cache hits

asi.bounded_resources: The change removes transient allocations and adds no retained state, queue, lock, or resource consumer.
asi.safety: Byte slicing uses checked access with saturating subtraction, so short and non-ASCII input cannot panic. Equivalence tests cover every action suffix, mixed case, method fallback, short strings, and non-ASCII input.
asi.summary: Authorization action classification now uses allocation-free case-insensitive byte checks instead of allocating lowercase operation and uppercase method strings.
asi.validation: Three eight-worker paired runs improved classification by 9.036505, 9.272416, and 9.127046 times. The final run black-boxed runtime input and sustained 1.8819 billion decisions per second versus 205.1 million before.

description: perf(kura): classify authorization actions without allocation
